exp0.h1: Designed and delivered the company's LLM orchestration architecture: an orchestrator routing requests across specialised agents, provider failover so one vendor outage cannot take the feature down, and a MongoDB layer for document retrieval, agent execution logs and a response cache that cuts repeat inference cost. Picked the provider by benchmarking five LLMs on cost, latency and output quality.
exp0.h2: Traced a core query's latency to stale planner statistics using EXPLAIN ANALYZE — the divergence between estimated and actual rows exposed a sequential scan chosen over an existing index. Refreshed the statistics, restored correct index usage and tuned autovacuum thresholds so it would not recur: 2s down to about 150ms, then documented the method for the team.
exp0.h3: Shifted releases from weekly batches to daily continuous deployment by introducing CI/CD with automated test suites — smaller changesets, cheaper rollbacks, lower risk per release.
exp0.h4: Authored the team's code review standard, now applied across every backend service: named the recurring anti-patterns and gave each one a concrete refactoring path.

exp1.context: Software consultancy · Brazilian and international clients
exp1.h1: Became sole technical owner of the company's greenfield social platform — NestJS, Next.js, PostgreSQL. Shipped 12 feature modules with no senior engineer above me, and set the technical direction the other three engineers on the build worked to.
exp1.h2: Built the recommendation engine from scratch — TF-IDF vectorisation with cosine similarity over user-generated content, ranking a personalised feed without any third-party ML service.
exp1.h3: Technical lead on international engagements, with requirements, code review and stakeholder communication conducted in English; drove Brazilian-market delivery directly alongside the Product Owner.

exp2.context: Footwear retail · internal financial and administrative systems
exp2.h1: Inherited an abandoned financial dashboard — revenue, cost and cash-flow reporting used from the operations floor up to the owners — with no handoff and no documentation. Reverse-engineered it, assessed the debt and set the migration strategy alone. Promoted within six months.
exp2.h2: Stabilised it on three fronts: eliminated the crashes that made it unreliable, traced and corrected the inconsistent figures it had been reporting, and cut load times — restoring confidence in numbers the business was already making decisions on.
exp2.h3: Migrated 40+ views to React over 15 months while the system stayed live and in daily use — incremental cutover, no feature freeze, no big-bang rewrite, no interruption to financial reporting.
exp2.h4: Rolled TypeScript across the full codebase after making the case to non-technical stakeholders, and automated Kubernetes deployments across dev, staging and production.

project1.description: SaaS platform that detects client churn 6–10 weeks in advance. Scores health signals from Google Ads and Meta Ads, runs a weight-learning engine per client, and generates AI-powered weekly briefs. Built with multi-tenant RLS, Stripe billing gates, and full observability.

project2.description: Approval gateway for AI agents: an API and MCP proxy that pauses risky tool calls until a human approves — declarative policy, approval by exception, and a hash-chained audit trail that verifies offline. Open-core: the local mode ships under Apache-2.0 on npm, the cloud adds multi-reviewer review, Slack and hosted audit.

project3.description: A scroll-led essay on the history of technology, told through eight artefacts — from a struck stone 3.3 million years ago to machines that are learning to judge. One WebGL point cloud is reassembled into every era's form, the interval between two eras sets the height of the silence before it, and a single accent walks the spectrum as you scroll. Lighthouse 100 on desktop and 99 on mobile with the artefact intact: the heavy layers wait for the reader's first move.

freelance.h1: Five or more concurrent client engagements through Workana, delivered alongside full-time roles.
freelance.h2: Cut a frontend Docker image from 1.9 GB to about 210 MB — a 89% reduction — by diagnosing the cause and rebuilding the pipeline with multi-stage builds, with no prior documentation to work from. Smaller artifacts dropped registry and transfer costs by over 60%.
freelance.h3: Built multi-provider authentication from the ground up — email, Google and Microsoft flows, 2FA, account recovery, PostgreSQL-backed hashing. No auth-related incidents reported post-launch.
freelance.h4: Shipped production Stripe billing for three client platforms — subscription flows and webhooks built for idempotency, so retries never double-charged.
